provenance.title: QUANTUM MODULARITY AND COMPLEX CHERN-SIMONS THEORY

candidates.statement: - The coefficients of $\phi^+_{K,\zeta}(\hbar)=\phi_{K,\zeta}(\hbar)/\phi_{K,\zeta}(0)$ should be elements of the field $F_K(\zeta)$, where $F_K$ is the trace field of $K$.

- The constant term (under some mild assumptions on $F_K(\zeta)$) should factor as follows: $$\label{eq.phi0factor} \phi_{K,k}(0) = \phi_{K,1}(0) \sqrt[k]{\varepsilon_K} \beta_{K,k}$$ where $\phi_{K,1}(0)^2 \in F_K(\zeta)$, $\varepsilon_K$ is a unit (i.e., an algebraic integer of norm $\pm 1$) in $F_K(\zeta)$ that depends only on the element of the Bloch group of $K$ (and $\zeta$), and $\beta_{K,k} \in F_K(\zeta)$.
Moreover, (local) triangulation-invariance of the level-$k$ state integral suggests that $S_{\gamma,n,k}$ should be independent of triangulation and $\gamma$ for all $n$.
In order for the path-integral measure $\exp(-iS)$ to be invariant under all gauge transformations of $\mathcal A$, the levels $t,\tilde t$ must obey the quantization condition

The Quantum Modularity Conjecture asserts that the exact element of $F_{K,k}$ should to have the form: $$\label{eq.xe} x^{\mathrm{exact}}_{k,\ell} = \varepsilon_{K,k} \beta_{K,k}^k$$ for $\varepsilon_{K,k} \in \mathcal O_{F_K(\zeta_k)}^{\times}$ (an algebraic unit) and $\beta_{K,k} \in F_K(\zeta_k)^\times$.
